title: Add multi-metric temporal-hedged canary orchestrator with tenant-weighted rollback policy
author: Maria Alvarez
description: Summary: Introduce a new orchestrator that evaluates candidate rollouts using a temporal-hedged, multi-metric decision process that hedges decisions across short-term spike signals and medium-term trends. Motivation: Existing canary detectors focus on single dominant signals (e.g., p95 latency) and trigger conservative rollbacks that either overreact to transient spikes or underreact to slow drifts. The new orchestrator combines several orthogonal signals (latency percentiles, throughput deltas, error-rate drift, and token-level tail latency) into a weighted decision surface that is temporally smoothed and hedged by probing sibling variants. It also adds a tenant-weighted rollback policy so multi-tenant deployments prioritize tenants with tighter SLOs when deciding cutover or throttle actions. Design: - Multi-metric fusion: normalized z-score fusion of configured metrics with configurable weights per feature flag. - Temporal hedging: short (1m), medium (10m), and long (60m) exponential smoothing windows; decisions require alignment across at least two windows or a hedged probe vote. - Hedged probing: when signals disagree, the orchestrator issues small, targeted probe traffic to candidate and baseline variants and computes a probe confidence. - Tenant weighting: rollback/quarantine budget is allocated proportionally to tenant SLO criticality and recent error exposure. - Rollout actions: allow staged cutover, pause, shrink, and immediate rollback with configurable quanta. Implementation: - New package: infra/canary/orchestrator with core engine, metric adapters, probe scheduler, and policy evaluators. - Integrations: metrics ingestion via observability/metrics-client; tracing hooks for attributions; console dashboards and per-route config UI. - Config surface: canary policies are expressed as YAML with fields: metrics, window_weights, probe_rate, tenant_priority_map, quorum_thresholds. Tests & results: - Local unit and integration tests added (canary engine, probe scheduler, policy evaluation). - Synthetic e2e runs against the perf-canary harness: 1200 simulated rollouts across three traffic shapes; true positive detection rate improved by 18% vs. existing canary, false positive reduced by 23% on bursty traffic. - Latency overhead: engine CPU < 2% tail at 50k checks/minute on a small sizing; probe traffic default limited to 0.5% of candidate traffic. Risk & mitigations: - Risk: miscalibrated tenant weights could bias decisions. Mitigation: safe defaults and a dry-run mode that logs decisions without enforcing actions. - Risk: probe-induced false negatives on very low-volume routes. Mitigation: minimum traffic floor and alternative passive heuristics. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (dry-run): deploy orchestrator in dry-run to 10% of routes for 1 week. - Stage 2 (observability): enable dashboard panels and alerting for disagreement cases. - Stage 3 (gradual cutover): enable automatic actions for low-risk routes, keep manual approval for enterprise routes. Checklist: - [x] Core engine impl and unit tests - [x] Probe scheduler + rate limiter - [x] Tenant weighting + config mapping - [x] Console config UI and dashboard panels - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary harness - [x] Docs: design doc and runbook - [x] Linear ticket ENG-11472 updated with rollout dates Related: ENG-11499 (add tenant SLO metadata pipeline), SUP-8271 incident follow-up notes Examples: included in examples/canary-scenarios/hedged-configs.yaml with four canonical traffic shapes. Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the metric fusion layer extensible so future ML-based ranking can be swapped in behind the same policy API.

review_comments: Ethan Park: Nice approach, can you justify the chosen smoothing windows? Are they tunable per-route?
Maria Alvarez: The 1/10/60 windows were chosen from perf-harness grid search; documented in the design doc and exposed as per-route overrides in the YAML; added notes to runbook.
Priya Desai: Concern: probe traffic could skew billing on Dedicated customers. Suggest adding billing-tier probe caps.
Maria Alvarez: Added tenant_priority_map to cap probe_rate per tenant and a global probe_budget feature flag; included unit tests around probe budgeting.
Lukas Meyer: CI flaky test 'canary_engine_integration_test' failed once, rerun passed. Please add a brief comment in the test explaining the non-determinism and how we simulate clocks.
Maria Alvarez: Added test comment and tightened fake clock bounds; reran CI and green.
release_notes: New orchestration mode: 'temporal-hedged' canary with multi-metric fusion, hedged probing, and tenant-weighted rollback policy. Default is dry-run. See docs/runbooks/canary-orchestrator.md for migration steps.
